name: Neutrope Source Updates Hub
author: Neutrope Inc.

sections.description:
Neutrope Source Updates Hub gives editors a dedicated place to manage short notes about trusted source updates. It is designed for sites that need to track policy changes, examination schedules, public notices, vendor release notes, or similar source-backed information without mixing those entries into ordinary blog posts.

The plugin is built around a source-first workflow:

  • Public output shows administrator-verified entries by default.
  • Entries require a Source URL and Source name before publication.
  • The optional verification requirement can prevent publication until an administrator confirms the source.
  • RSS / Atom ingestion never publishes automatically.
  • Generated entries are unverified drafts with empty post content and excerpt.
  • No AI summaries, telemetry, tracking, external JavaScript, or external CSS are included.

Main features:

  • Custom post type ntoh_official_news for short source notes.
  • Source URL, source name, published date, checked date, importance, pinned, archived, verified, and internal-note metadata.
  • Category and tag taxonomies for source notes.
  • Admin columns for source, dates, importance, verification, pinned, archived, and source URL.
  • [ntoh_news_hub] shortcode with list, cards, and compact layouts.
  • [ntoh_news_hub_grouped] shortcode for grouped category or tag sections.
  • Settings for default layout, default limit, link target, archived behavior, verified-only display, noindex on single pages, frontend CSS loading, summaries, single-page redirects, and publish validation.
  • Administrator-enabled RSS / Atom source records.
  • Candidate and fetch-log admin screens.
  • Review status, risk labels, source health, Overview, filtered review lists, and dismissible admin notices for review-needed items.

External services

This plugin can make outbound HTTPS requests only after an administrator creates and enables a source record.

The plugin requests only the RSS / Atom feed URL configured by the administrator and processes up to the latest three items per run. It does not request or monitor any other web pages.

Feed requests use:

  • HTTPS only.
  • No redirects.
  • A 10-second timeout.
  • A 2 MB response limit.
  • WordPress safe HTTP URL checks.
  • An exact allowed domain for item URLs taken from the feed.

The request User-Agent contains the plugin name, plugin version, and site URL for normal HTTP identification. The plugin does not contact unrelated services.

Privacy / Stored data

The plugin does not send telemetry and does not track visitors or administrators.

Stored data may include:

  • Source note posts and their metadata.
  • Administrator-created source records.
  • RSS / Atom candidate metadata, including source URL, canonical URL, title, GUID hash, date, and a private plain-text review excerpt of up to 500 characters.
  • Fetch logs with run status and error messages.
  • Per-user admin notice dismiss signatures for review-needed notices.

Posts generated from RSS / Atom items are created as unverified drafts with empty content and excerpt. The plugin does not automatically publish generated entries.

The plugin does not delete its custom tables or post meta when it is updated.

Upgrading from the pre-directory version

Back up the database and plugin files first. The directory name has changed, so this package is installed alongside the old package, not over it. Deactivate the old core before activating this plugin; do not delete its data. Do not run both cores together.

Activation migrates the legacy post type and taxonomies in place, keeping IDs, metadata and term relationships. Stored legacy shortcode tags in posts, excerpts and standard text/HTML/block widgets are updated to [ntoh_news_hub] and [ntoh_news_hub_grouped]. Update hard-coded theme calls, custom integrations, saved admin URLs and externally stored shortcode text manually. Existing pretty permalink paths are retained.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the neutrope-source-updates-hub folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the ZIP from the WordPress admin upload screen.
  2. Activate the plugin from the Plugins screen.
  3. Add source notes under the “公式情報メモ” admin menu.
  4. Place [ntoh_news_hub] on a page or post where the list should appear.
  5. Optional: create administrator-enabled RSS / Atom sources under the source settings screen.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin publish fetched items automatically?

No. RSS / Atom ingestion creates only unverified drafts or review candidates. An administrator must review the source and publish manually.

Can I use the plugin without remote requests?

Yes. If no source records are enabled, the plugin can be used as a manual source-note manager and shortcode display tool.

Does the plugin scrape or monitor web pages?

No. The plugin requests only RSS / Atom feed URLs that an administrator configured and enabled. It does not fetch, scrape, or monitor other web pages.

Can I show only urgent or pinned items?

Use shortcode attributes such as [ntoh_news_hub importance="urgent"]. Pinned items sort to the top.

Why does a category shortcode show no results?

The category and tag attributes use taxonomy slugs, not visible names. Edit the term and use its slug in the shortcode.

Will my theme styles be affected?

Frontend classes are prefixed with .ntoh-. You can also disable the bundled frontend CSS from the settings page.
sections.changelog:
0.5.0

  • Rename the plugin and text domain to Neutrope Source Updates Hub.
  • Scope validation and fetch feedback to plugin administration screens.
  • Prefix post type, taxonomy and shortcode names; migrate existing stored data without changing object IDs.
  • Guard against running the old and renamed core together.

0.4.1

  • Enqueue admin scripts and styles through WordPress APIs.
  • Sanitize submitted fields on input and reject unexpected input types.
  • Use the feed API already loaded by WordPress.

0.4.0

  • Removed the web page change-monitoring source type. Sources now use RSS / Atom feeds only.
  • Existing records created by the removed source type are kept, shown as an unavailable source type, and skipped by scheduled fetches. No data is deleted.
  • Added filters for source types and admin summary display so the review workflow can be extended.

0.3.0

  • Added review status and risk labels for candidates.
  • Added source health metadata for source records.
  • Added the Neutrope Source Updates Hub Overview screen.
  • Added filters for candidates and fetch logs.
  • Added source, candidate, draft, official URL, and fetch-log navigation links.
  • Added admin notices for review-needed items.
  • Added dismissible per-user notice state.
  • No auto-publish is included.
  • No AI summaries are included.

0.2.1

  • Internal development release. Its source type was removed in 0.4.0.

0.2.0

  • Added administrator-enabled HTTPS RSS / Atom ingestion.
  • Added private source records, candidates, fetch logs, manual fetch controls, Cron dispatch, locks, duplicate checks, and retention cleanup.
  • Automated entries are always unverified drafts with empty content and excerpt.

0.1.7

  • Added listing-first display refinements, category chips, optional empty published-date rows, summary display controls, and shortcode class support.

0.1.6

  • Fixed use_single_page=0 redirects to reach the stored source URL.

0.1.5

  • Added the list layout, offset shortcode attribute, single-page redirect setting, and optional relaxation of the verification publish blocker.

0.1.4

  • Updated frontend display so the source URL CTA is the primary public link and fixed ZIP packaging path separators.

0.1.3

  • Added grouped shortcode support and frontend display refinements.

0.1.2

  • Improved taxonomy slug documentation and publish-block notices.

0.1.1

  • Added administrator verification metadata, default verified-only public display, and publish guard behavior.

0.1.0

  • Initial release.
